prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
**[goal]** A single-file Windows-95-style archery level at `./game/index.html` — mouse-aimed bow with draw-for-power, balloons, score, start, and a loss condition.

**[action]** Wrote the whole game in one file (no build, only external dependency is the "Press Start 2P" Google Font), then opened it in the browser and played it via scripted mouse input.

**[result]** What's in it and how it plays:
- **Look**: pixel-font HUD, dusk-to-night gradient sky with twinkling stars, moon, rolling grass hills; glossy balloons with strings and highlights; a little archer whose bow, string and nocked arrow visibly pull back as you hold the button (a draw meter fills and flashes green at full power).
- **Feel**: arrows take a slight gravity arc, balloon wobble makes aim matter, particle bursts + floating "+N" score text on pops, screen-shake on the lives HUD when a balloon escapes, combo multiplier (consecutive pops without a miss), rare gold ★ balloon worth 30×combo.
- **Sound**: all WebAudio, zero assets — bow creak while drawing, pitch-shifted twang on release scaled to power, pop pitch rises with your combo, gold chime, descending horn when a balloon escapes, last-10-second ticks, win/lose jingles.
- **Rules**: 60-second round; 3 escaped balloons = Game Over screen with score, accuracy and best combo; survive the clock = Level Clear.

**Assumptions I chose**: lose by escapes (keeps pressure on aim, not speed), win by surviving the timer, combos reset on a missed shot, touch input mapped to the same hold-and-release controls.

**How I know it's right**: verified live in the browser — menu, in-play screenshot showed SCORE 120, timer counting, arrows in flight and lives dropping on escapes; a full run reached the GAME OVER screen (score 180, accuracy 28%, best combo x4); zero JS console errors; PLAY AGAIN reset score/time to 0/60. Browser tab closed afterward.
